A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Augmented Spectral Feature Learning work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting, reordering, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic IV, dSprites, and off-policy evaluation results, together with alignment, parameter-sensitivity, and higher-rank experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds delta-selection experiments and comparisons with a naive outcome-aware baseline in Appendices E.9 and G.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a conservative alignment-based selection rule: scan increasing delta values and accept an increase only when estimated alignment improves by at least 5% (Appendices E.9 and G). v1 discussed alignment-based tuning heuristically. The augmented losses, 2SLS estimator, OPE iteration, and higher-rank extension remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic IV regression, the heart and ellipse dSprites tasks, and Cartpole, Mountain Car, and Catch OPE. The added tuning and baseline studies reuse existing task coverage; their parameter grids and sample sizes concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds an evaluated naive outcome-aware comparator that learns outcome-predictive Z-features and then predicts them from X. SpecIV, DFIV, and KIV remain in their original comparisons. Bruns-Smith's method is discussed but is not directly benchmarked.

E3.justification: Additional experiments evaluate automatic delta selection. Appendix G specifies 15,000 training and 5,000 evaluation samples, noise variance 0.2, and a post-hoc rejection rule for predictions whose standard deviation exceeds five times that of Y. These are additional protocols; the original benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.9 adds practical tests of alignment-based delta selection on synthetic and dSprites data. Appendix G adds a substantial investigation of whether simpler outcome-aware learning suffices, examining MSE tails and unstable-model rejection across parameter grids. The earlier alignment and rank-two perturbation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new baseline study explicitly reports median, 5th-percentile, and 95th-percentile MSEs and fitted-model counts. Existing dSprites run counts and the five-run OPE mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish increased replication of those experiments.

E6.justification: New Figures 14–15 report alignment-selected prediction errors; Figures 17–19 report comparable naive-baseline median errors but heavier tails and frequent rejection, versus 9 rejected AugSpecIV fits out of 1,200. Figure 4 revises displayed alignment distributions. Figure 3 removes v1's h_new median MSE of 61.16 at delta = 3. These additions and revisions do not establish an across-version performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the claimed attained loss bound to use the rank-d truncated operator's squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm and states the augmented spectral-gap assumption. New Proposition A.4 proves a population excess-loss-to-operator-gap bound. Appendices B and E.9 add boundedness/compactness and alignment-conditioning derivations, while existing proofs receive algebraic corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: outcome-aware spectral learning addresses misalignment, admits theoretical error analysis, and works on synthetic, dSprites, and OPE benchmarks. The additional theory and experiments strengthen support without redefining these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains instability of the alignment estimator at large delta and shifts advice toward conservative alignment-based selection. Appendix E.7.2 qualifies compactness of the modified OPE operator as an assumption, replacing v1's categorical assertion. Appendix G explains why outcome-predictive features alone can fail to recover the structural function.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly supplies a reproduction-code repository location. Table 6 and Appendix G document the naive baseline's five-feature architecture and its tuning and rejection procedures. Existing architecture and OPE hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive comparison with Bruns-Smith (2025), distinguishing representation learning, convergence conditions, and post-hoc checks. It also adds Bennett et al. (2025) and Shen et al. (2026) to the saddle-point literature. The overall positioning around SpecIV remains.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, the delta-selection discussion is reordered, and explanatory prose and notation are refined. v2 also adds impact and funding statements and updates affiliations and citation style. Most existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to an ICML two-column layout. Existing plots are resized and reformatted, Figure 4's panels are reversed, and appendix displays are rearranged. Five new result figures and Table 6 are added; v1's rank-two Figure 14 is retained as v2's Figure 16.

improvement.justification: The corrected loss optimum and new Proposition A.4 materially strengthen the theoretical connection between training loss and operator error. Appendices E.9 and G address important practical gaps through tests of delta selection and simpler outcome-aware alternatives, supported by new code-access information. These gains outweigh the loss of the high-delta numerical annotation, although end-to-end DNN optimization and generalization guarantees remain open.
